body:
![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

Piping `Get-VHD` directly to `Get-Disk` can fail because `Get-Disk` does not have pipeline binding for the `VirtualHardDisk` type, and its `-Path` parameter expects a physical device path rather than a VHDX file path. Instead, explicitly retrieve the `DiskNumber` from the VHD object and pass it to `Get-Disk -Number`.

```
        $vhd = Get-VHD -Path $seedPath
        if ($null -eq $vhd.DiskNumber) { throw 'VHD is not mounted or disk number not found.' }
        $seedDisk = Get-Disk -Number $vhd.DiskNumber
```

<details>
<summary>References</summary>

1. In PowerShell scripts designed to be executed in interactive sessions, avoid using the 'exit' command to signal failures, as it terminates the entire PowerShell host process and closes the user's terminal. Instead, use 'throw' to signal validation or execution failures, which preserves failure semantics without terminating the interactive host.
</details>

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

Under strict mode (`Set-StrictMode -Version Latest`), referencing a non-existent property on an object throws a runtime exception. If the GitHub API response `$before` is null or does not contain the `workflow_runs` property, accessing `$before.workflow_runs` will crash the script. Explicitly verify that the property exists on the object before accessing it.

```
        $before = Invoke-ControllerGitHubApi -Token $installationToken -Endpoint "repos/$repository/actions/workflows/$([string]$config.github.isolated_workflow_file)/runs?event=workflow_dispatch&branch=$([string]$decision.default_branch)&per_page=20"
        $knownRunIds = @()
        if ($null -ne $before -and $before.PSObject.Properties['workflow_runs']) {
            $knownRunIds = @($before.workflow_runs | ForEach-Object { [long]$_.id })
        }
```

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

Under strict mode (`Set-StrictMode -Version Latest`), referencing a non-existent property on an object throws a runtime exception. If the GitHub API response `$runs` is null or does not contain the `workflow_runs` property, accessing `$runs.workflow_runs` will crash the script. Explicitly verify that the property exists on the object before accessing it.

```
            $runs = Invoke-ControllerGitHubApi -Token $installationToken -Endpoint "repos/$repository/actions/workflows/$([string]$config.github.isolated_workflow_file)/runs?event=workflow_dispatch&branch=$([string]$decision.default_branch)&per_page=20"
            $newRuns = @()
            if ($null -ne $runs -and $runs.PSObject.Properties['workflow_runs']) {
                $newRuns = @($runs.workflow_runs | Where-Object { $knownRunIds -notcontains [long]$_.id } | Sort-Object {[DateTime]$_.created_at})
            }
            if ($newRuns.Count -eq 1) { $runId = [long]$newRuns[0].id }
            elseif ($newRuns.Count -gt 1) { throw 'Multiple new workflow runs appeared; exact pilot run binding is ambiguous.' }
```

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Refresh the installation token during long pilots**

When the dispatched workflow runs near its configured 60-minute timeout, this 65-minute polling window keeps using the same installation token minted before VM creation/bootstrapping. [GitHub's REST docs](https://docs.github.com/rest/apps/apps) state installation tokens expire after one hour and expired tokens return 401 requiring a new token, so a long-but-valid pilot can fail polling and then fail cancel/runner cleanup/reporting with the same expired token; refresh the installation token before the one-hour mark or keep the controller wait below the token lifetime.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Page through runner inventory before cleanup**

In repositories with more than 100 self-hosted runners, this only checks the first page before deciding whether to delete the JIT runner. GitHub's runner list API is paginated with `per_page` capped at 100 and a separate `page` parameter, so a residual runner outside the first page is reported as absent and never deleted; page through the inventory or issue the delete by ID and handle 404.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Drain lifecycle output before waiting**

If a lifecycle PowerShell invocation emits enough stdout or stderr, waiting for process exit before reading either redirected stream can cause the child to block on a full pipe; Microsoft documents this `WaitForExit`-before-`ReadToEnd` pattern as a deadlock risk. In that case the helper reports `lifecycle_timeout` and kills an otherwise diagnosable create/attach/start/destroy attempt, so drain the streams asynchronously or before waiting.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Cancel runs even when discovery misses them**

When `workflow_dispatch` succeeds but the new run is not visible within the 2-minute, first-20-runs discovery window, `$runId` stays null and this guard skips cancellation altogether. The VM is then destroyed while the workflow remains queued on a one-off runner label until GitHub times it out, leaving stale Actions state and potentially blocking same-SHA workflow concurrency; keep enough dispatch/discovery state to find and cancel the run before teardown.
